title: Problem Overview
content: Erdős Problem #481: For affine maps with Σ(1/aᵢ) > 1, iterating T(A) = (aᵢxⱼ + bᵢ) from A₁=(1) must eventually produce repeated elements. Solved by Klarner (1982) using semigroup theory.
mathContext: The problem appears in Erdős-Graham (1980, p.96). They remarked 'it is surprising that [this problem] offers difficulty.' The simple statement hides subtle connections to algebraic semigroup theory.
prerequisites: affine maps on the natural numbers

title: Affine Transformation
content: The map x ↦ ax + b for natural numbers a, b. These are the building blocks - each (aᵢ, bᵢ) pair defines one transformation applied to each sequence element.
mathContext: See annotation content for formal details of affine transformation
prerequisites: affine functions of the form x ↦ ax + b

title: Affine Parameters
content: The AffineParams structure bundles r transformations with their (aᵢ, bᵢ) pairs. The constraint aᵢ > 0 ensures the transformations are non-degenerate.
mathContext: See annotation content for formal details of affine parameters

title: The Density Condition
content: Σ(1/aᵢ) > 1 is the crucial condition. It measures the 'coverage density' of the transformations. When > 1, there's enough overlap to force collisions. The condition is tight: Σ(1/aᵢ) ≤ 1 allows avoidance.
mathContext: Think of [0, N] being covered by intervals of length N/aᵢ. If Σ(1/aᵢ) > 1, the total coverage exceeds N, so pigeonhole guarantees overlaps. Examples: r=2, a₁=a₂=2 gives Σ=1 (boundary); r=3, a₁=a₂=a₃=2 gives Σ=3/2>1 (applies).
prerequisites: covering [0, N] by intervals of length N/aᵢ

title: The T Operator
content: T(A) applies each transformation to each element: T(A) = (aᵢxⱼ + bᵢ). If A has n elements, T(A) has rn elements. The sequence grows exponentially.
mathContext: See annotation content for formal details of the t operator
prerequisites: applying a family of maps to every element

title: Initial Sequence
content: A₁ = (1), the singleton list containing just 1. This is the seed from which all subsequent sequences are generated by applying T.
mathContext: See annotation content for formal details of initial sequence
prerequisites: singleton sequences as a starting seed

title: Iterate T
content: iterateT defines Aₖ = T^{k-1}(A₁). The sequence grows as: A₁ has 1 element, A₂ has r, A₃ has r², etc. Length grows exponentially as r^{k-1}.
mathContext: $|A_k| = r^{k-1}$; elements of $A_k$ are all values of form $a_{i_1} a_{i_2} \cdots a_{i_{k-1}} + b_{i_1}(a_{i_2}\cdots) + \ldots$ (compositions of $k-1$ affine maps applied to 1).
prerequisites: compositions of affine maps applied to 1

title: Has Repeats
content: hasRepeats(seq) is true when some value appears at least twice in the sequence. This is what the theorem asserts must eventually happen.
mathContext: See annotation content for formal details of has repeats
prerequisites: detecting duplicate elements in a sequence

title: Erdős-Graham Conjecture (Proved)
content: If Σ(1/aᵢ) > 1, then some iterate Aₖ must have repeated elements. Klarner (1982) proved this via free semigroup theory: the density condition characterizes when the affine semigroup is non-free, and non-freeness implies relations that manifest as collisions. When Σ(1/aᵢ) ≤ 1, the semigroup IS free and collisions can be avoided.
mathContext: The axiom captures the deep result of Klarner's 1982 paper. The proof technique connects number theory to algebraic semigroup theory - a connection Erdős and Graham found surprising.

title: Klarner's Theorem
content: klarner_theorem formalizes that the Erdős-Graham conjecture is true. The proof is a direct application of the axiom. Kolpakov-Talambutsa (2022) extended this to more general settings, including affine maps on the real line.
mathContext: See annotation content for formal details of klarner's theorem
prerequisites: formalizing the Erdős-Graham conjecture as a theorem
Kolpakov-Talambutsa extension to the real line

title: Summary Theorem
content: erdos_481_summary restates Klarner's theorem as the complete resolution of Problem #481. The density condition Σ(1/aᵢ) > 1 is both necessary and sufficient for eventual collisions in affine sequence iteration.
mathContext: See annotation content for formal details of summary theorem
